query:
The group agreed to attend a full family weekend in February half term. What did Callum's response to that decision reveal about his actual position, and what specifically in the way he responded tells you that?

Options:
A. Margaret
B. Callum
C. Rachel
D. Jamie
context:
[1] (about=Callum, episodic, t6 @2026-01-25T11:58:00) That tracks. Family estrangement as a late-stage outcome is documented to be deeply regretted by most parties. I will come.
[2] (about=Rachel, episodic, t5 @2026-01-25T11:30:00) I want to propose something. February half term. Mum and Dad's, full weekend. I will organise it. Everyone should be there. Callum, I know that is a stretch but I would appreciate it.
[3] (about=Callum, episodic, t12 @2026-02-15T15:38:00) Edinburgh is quite isolated when it is not going well. More than I had factored in. I think I needed the February weekend more than I knew at the time.
[4] (about=Callum, episodic, t10 @2026-02-08T21:07:00) I am choosing not to respond to that.
[5] (about=Callum, episodic, t14 @2026-02-22T18:46:00) I had anticipated that.
[6] (about=Callum, episodic, t14 @2026-02-22T19:17:00) I will be in Manchester for Easter. For what it's worth.
[7] (about=Rachel, episodic, t8 @2026-02-01T10:11:00) Dad, how long are they saying? Is it sorted this week ahead of the weekend?
[8] (about=Callum, episodic, t12 @2026-02-15T15:51:00) ...You read that.
[9] (about=Callum, episodic, t10 @2026-02-08T21:02:00) That did not happen.
[10] (about=Jamie, episodic, t8 @2026-02-01T10:19:00) dad on the tram, genuinely a sentence i didn't expect to read. how was it?
agent_answer:
**Answer: B. Callum**

Callum's response revealed that his actual position was **emotionally detached and reluctant rather than enthusiastic** — he agreed to attend, but on rational/clinical grounds, not out of genuine desire.

**What specifically tells you this:** In excerpt [1], instead of expressing any warmth or personal feeling, he frames the decision in abstract, third‑person, intellectualized language: *"Family estrangement as a late-stage outcome is documented to be deeply regretted by most parties. I will come."* The phrasing "That tracks" plus the citation-style observation about "documented" research and "most parties" shows he processed the invitation like an academic conclusion, not a heartfelt choice — his flat "I will come" follows the reasoning, not emotion.

This is later confirmed by his own admission in excerpt [3]: *"I think I needed the February weekend more than I knew at the time"* — indicating that at the moment of responding he did not fully register his need, consistent with the detached way he first agreed.
